speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this cough going on for about two months now. It usually brings up some clear sputum, but I haven't coughed up any blood. However, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very specific request, but I must first determine the cause of your symptoms before I can provide any classification. Have you noticed any fever, night sweats, or unintended weight loss alongside your cough?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't noticed any fever, night sweats, or weight loss. The cough seems to get worse at night, and I do get short of breath when I try to do physical work. I want to emphasize that, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand the need for a classification, but I must first identify the underlying cause to ensure the code is accurate. Since your symptoms worsen at night and cause shortness of breath with exertion, have you noticed any wheezing or a tightness in your chest? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hyperinflation noted, no focal infiltrates or masses.

speaker: Doctor
text: The chest X-ray showing hyperinflation without focal infiltrates strongly suggests an obstructive airway issue. Given your two-month history of cough, clear sputum, and symptoms worsening at night, have you noticed any seasonal allergies or exposure to dust and chemicals?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I have a history of seasonal allergies, and since I work as a landscaper, I am frequently exposed to dust and chemicals. I don't think I have any wheezing, but the shortness of breath definitely gets worse when I'm exerting myself.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of seasonal allergies, occupational exposure to dust and chemicals, and the X-ray findings of hyperinflation, do you have a family history of asthma or allergies? REQUEST TEST: Spirometry with bronchodilator reversibility DIAGNOSIS READY: Asthma
